chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskān who said: He narrated to me Sa'īd from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him)
From a man who bequeathed a Hajj, so his executor made it for one person. He said: 'The executor bears the cost and dedicates it to a Hajj as he bequeathed,
for indeed Allah, the Exalted, says: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then the sin is upon those who alter it.'"
I said: 'And whoever bequeaths twenty dirhams for a Hajj?' He said: 'A man performs Hajj with it, from wherever it suffices.'

key_terms.حَجَّة: A Hajj pilgrimage (specifically one person's Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an executor uses a bequest for Hajj for fewer people than intended?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiduciary duty of an executor (wasi) who misapplies funds designated for Hajj, establishing that the shortfall is deducted from the executor's own share of the estate to ensure the testator's specific intent is fulfilled. By citing the verse on altering divine decrees, the Imam underscores the sanctity of adhering to the precise terms of a bequest, while the ruling for smaller sums demonstrates the flexibility in applying funds to a single pilgrim when the amount is insufficient for multiple individuals.
